title: Error thrown when using Dictionary.has with mismatching type on typed dictionaries
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.4.stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.3.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Pro (Apple7) - Apple M1 Pro (10 threads)

### Issue description

When using the `has` method on a typed dictionary with a parameter that doesn't match the type of the dictionary's keys, the engine throws an error

```
E 0:00:00:803   main.gd:9 @ _ready(): Attempted to use 'has' a variable of type 'String' into a TypedDictionary.Key of type 'int'.
  <C++ Error>   Method/function failed. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  ./core/variant/container_type_validate.h:103 @ validate()
  <Stack Trace> main.gd:9 @ _ready()
```

```
E 0:00:00:803   main.gd:9 @ _ready(): Condition "!_p->typed_key.validate(key, "use 'has'")" is true. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  core/variant/dictionary.cpp:210 @ has()
  <Stack Trace> main.gd:9 @ _ready()
```

While this might make sense in paper, it's extremely limiting since a lot of utilities that work with dictionaries are meant to work with any kind of dictionary and shouldn't break if a user decides to type their dictionaries.

The specific use case (for context) is a deserializer that treats dictionaries in a special way if they contain a specific key. For example

```python
func deserialize(value: Dictionary) -> Variant:
  if not value.has("__type"):
    return deserialize_dict(value)
  
  match value.__type:
    "Foo":
      return deserialize_foo(value)
    "Bar":
      return deserialize_bar(value)
    # ... etc
```

This method is intended to work with any dictionary, but it will now break if the value passed is `Dictionary[int, Variant]` for example

I understand validating typed dictionary assignments, but `has` (and `get` as well) seems overzealous and wrong.

### Steps to reproduce

1) Call `has` on a dictionary with typed keys passing a value that doesn't match the type of the dictionary's keys

E.g.

```python
var dict: Dictionary[int, String] = {
  1: "Foo"
}

if dict.has("bar"):
  print("Hooray!")
```

That's it, no more steps. For context on why this is a problem, look at the previous section

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[typed-dictionary-has.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19711675/typed-dictionary-has.zip)

Open the project and just run it, you should see the errors in the debug console. The relevant script is `res://main.gd`
